items.note: Maximum temperature 1901-2001: in winter nine stations (including Vidisha) showed persistence and, except Jalaun, all 11 stations showed an increasing trend; summer showed no trend.
Trend slopes are very low; basin-average statistics show no significant trend in rainy or summer maximum temperature but an increasing trend in winter maximum temperature.
Minimum temperature 1901-2001: all stations show a significant increasing trend in winter and summer, though slope and relative change values are low.
Basin-average statistics show a significant increasing trend in summer and winter minimum temperature in the Betwa basin.
Decreasing rainy days at Tikamgarh, Begumganj and Khurai without a rainfall trend indicates increasing average rainfall intensity, with impact on run-off and ground water recharge.
Delayed onset of monsoon at Tikamgarh and Shivpuri could significantly affect planning of the Kharif crop.
Rising winter temperature with delayed OEM increases water demand, requires additional water supply, and delay in Kharif crop will affect the Rabi crop.
Conclusion: no trend in seasonal and yearly rainfall except a decreasing trend in summer rainfall at five stations; decrease in rainfall may lead to low crop productivity in the Betwa basin.
Minimum temperature increased at all stations in summer; winter maximum and minimum temperatures increase at all stations; this may change the growth stages and water use of winter wheat.
